text:
olivia_support: 🚨 customers reporting 5xx + timeouts to the hosted inference API (usa-east). Multiple support tickets, several high-value customers. I’m opening this thread to triage — please join if you’re free. sample error from a customer: `504 Gateway Timeout` and `upstream prematurely closed connection`.

devon_sre: thanks — on it. Can you paste a couple of request IDs or sample curl payloads? Are they all hitting the same model / route?

olivia_support: one sample req_id=8c4f2a, model=redwood-13b-quant, route=/v1/complete. curl from customer:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-quant","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```

errors in logs: `upstream error: connection reset by peer`, `context deadline exceeded`.

ajay_infra: seeing error spike on gateway metrics at 18:05 UTC — 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% -> 8% and p99 latency rose from 220ms -> 3.1s for the /v1/complete route. Backend pods for the 13b quant group show increased restart count on node gpunode-27.

marco_ml: model-serving telemetry shows KV cache saturation on a few pods (cache miss storm) and GC thrashing after a recent runtime patch. We're seeing OOMKilled on a subset of 13b-quant containers.

tess_prod: any recent deploys? I pushed a runtime tweak earlier this morning to change the memory config on the quant runtime (can revert if it's the cause).

nora_engineering: confirmed — there was a canary rolled at 09:30 that updated the runtime memory tuning kernel. Canary passed for low-traffic models but didn't exercise large-sequence workloads. Rolling that back now to canary-previous.

incident-bot: @channel incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-13 — Hosted inference 5xx/timeouts (Severity P1). War room link: https://remedy/INC-2026-03-15-13

devon_sre: mitigation plan (immediate):
- rollback runtime memory tweak (nora doing)
- temporarily route heavy/enterprise customers to redwood-7b-quant fallback via policy (tess + ajay)
- increase replicas for 13b pool by 30% to absorb in-flight work (ajay)
- raise gateway upstream timeout from 30s -> 60s as a short stopgap (devon)

ajay_infra: warming new replicas now and cordoning affected nodes. Patching autoscaler to favor scaling earlier on queued requests. ETA for extra replicas ~4m.

marco_ml: also enabling prefix KV caching on the critical routes to reduce repeated prefix work.

olivia_support: notify impacted customers: I’ll send templated update, offer failover to smaller model + credits. Sam, can you coordinate comms for the top 3 accounts?

sam_sales: on it — drafting messages and will post to the ticket queue. Will also offer a 10% credit for downtime.

devon_sre: logs snippet from gateway at spike peak:

```
[18:06:12] upstream_timeout: client=10.2.3.45 req_id=8c4f2a route=/v1/complete upstream=10.4.5.12:8080 status=502
[18:06:13] error: connection reset by peer
[18:06:15] context deadline exceeded
```

nora_engineering: rollback completed on canary; starting progressive rollback to stable. Observability: canary error rate was 1.3% but the large-sequence traffic multipliers made it 7.8% on 13b pools.

ajay_infra: extra replicas are up. Gateway timeout bumped to 60s. Routing policy change to redirect enterprise accounts to 7b fallback applied (canary first, then global).

marco_ml: after fallback and extra capacity p99 latency back to ~350ms for fallback model. 13b pool still experiencing a few restarts but overall error rate dropping from 8% -> 1.2%.

tess_prod: I’ll revert the config permanently and send a PR with safer memory defaults + e2e load test cases for large sequences.

olivia_support: customer-facing update — posted status at 18:20 UTC. Most customers accepted fallback while we stabilize. A few asked for SLA credits.

devon_sre: setting temporary mitigation closed-loop: keep the fallback routing until 13b pod restarts == 0 for 15min and p99 < 500ms.

marco_ml: note: we observed GC pressure tied to the new kernel scheduling change in the runtime. Action item: add canary load tests that simulate long-context inference for any runtime tweak.

nora_engineering: postmortem notes so far: root cause = unsafe runtime memory tuning change that reduced headroom under large sequence loads. Contributing factors: insufficient canary load coverage, autoscaler thresholds tuned for normal traffic pattern.

olivia_support: rubber-stamp for next steps? I'll create postmortem doc and link it to the incident ticket.

devon_sre: action items (assignments):
- nora_engineering: revert validated and add canary large-seq e2e tests (due EOD).
- tess_prod: update runtime memory defaults and add alerts for cache thrash/OOM (due +2 days).
- ajay_infra: adjust autoscaler policy and add surge capacity for critical models (due +3 days).
- marco_ml: implement KV cache metrics and automated rehydrate logic (due +5 days).
- olivia_support: draft customer post-incident notes and SLA credit plan (due +1 day).

nora_engineering: acknowledging. I'll attach failing canary logs and commit the test harness by EOD.

tess_prod: will open PR for memory defaults and add the alert rules. marking as blocker for next runtime release.

sam_sales: I'll prepare formal comms for impacted customers and coordinate credits with finance.

olivia_support: thanks everyone. closing war room once metrics stable for 30 minutes and all rollback checks green. leaving this thread for final postmortem link and action item tracking.

incident-bot: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-13 status: mitigated -> monitoring. follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

nora_engineering: final note — please add any logs or customer repros here. We need concrete reproducer for the GC scenario; marco, can you help capture heap profiles during a controlled run?

marco_ml: yes — will run controlled load and attach heap profiles to the postmortem.

olivia_support: added the incident to the support escalation board and linked all tickets. I'll update the postmortem doc with the timeline tomorrow.

devon_sre: will keep monitoring. If error rate rebounds, escalate to on-call infra manager. Good job all. :thumbsup?
